messages:
Anika: Heads-up — I pushed a quick panel into the observability dashboard that rolls up prefix cache coverage, token-saved, and per-customer hit-rate for the last 6h. URL: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/xyz/prefix-coverage :eyes:
Anika: Early signal — model 'redwood-7b-v2' shows a 12% drop in prefix hit-rate on route /chat/assist after the batching kernel change last night. Token-saved down ~22k tokens/hr for a handful of mid-market tenants.
matt: On it. Which kernel param changed? Was it the continuous-batch window tweak?
dilip: yeah matt — we reduced batch_hold_ms from 12 -> 6 to improve p50 on short seqs. That could reduce aggregation for common prefixes.
Anika: Exactly. The dashboard slice shows the hit-rate delta is concentrated in 3 customers that have high repetition in prompts. Per-route heatmap attached in the panel shows model+route spike.
rafael: Can you paste the raw query you used for the token-saved metric? Want to run the same against staging.
Anika: Here — the panel uses the derived metric:
```
SELECT model, route, customer_id,
  sum(tokens_saved) AS tokens_saved,
  avg(prefix_hitrate) AS avg_hitrate
FROM prefix_cache_telemetry
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY model, route, customer_id
ORDER BY tokens_saved DESC
```
sre-jen: ops-bot just posted a deploy at 2791234500 (kernel-change-v3). Could correlate timing.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline: kernel-change-v3 deployed to prod at 2026-03-17T21:55:00Z by matt. :white_check_mark:
matt: Thanks — reproducing locally: when batch_hold_ms is 6 I can see more fragmented KV cache keys for long prefixes due to earlier evictions on small batches. That explains hit-rate drop.
dilip: Hypothesis: smaller batch window reduces KV cache accumulation because fewer prefixes are seen by the same worker before a flush, causing less effective warmup.
Anika: Proposed mitigations: 1) temporarily revert batch_hold_ms for routes with >10% hit-rate drop, 2) enable per-route warmup (prefetch top-k prefixes for known tenants), 3) add kernel-side feature flag to prefer cache-friendlier batching for seq-length distribution > threshold.
rafael: I like option 2 as quick win. I can add a small prefetch job that runs every 5m for the top routes and pushes warmup keys to the worker-level cache. Do we have the top-key extraction query?
Anika: Yes — the dashboard back-end already exports top prefixes per route. Query snippet:
```
SELECT route, prefix_hash, count(*) AS freq
FROM request_prefixes
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY route, prefix_hash
ORDER BY freq DESC
LIMIT 500
```
matt: For the kernel change roll-forward plan: if we don't see latency improvement for p50 after 2 hours but see hit-rate < baseline and token-saved loss > 10k/hr, rollback. I'll add an automated check to the rollout job.
sre-jen: Add alert: pref-cache.tokens_saved.delta < -10000 over 1h AND pref-cache.hitrate.delta < -0.08 for any customer -> page oncall and notify eng-runtime.
dilip: Also want to capture profiling traces showing per-kernel queueing. I pushed a lightweight sampler to the runtime that annotates traces with batch_size_hist and kernel_choice. Can feed that to the panel as an annotation layer.
Anika: Nice. Action items: @matt -> add rollback guard to deploy job; @rafael -> prototype prefetch task for top 500 prefixes; @dilip -> surface kernel-choice annotation in dashboard; @sre-jen -> create alert rule and escalation; @Anika -> clean up dashboard panels and add a README explaining the tokens_saved metric.
Anika: Any objections to flipping batch_hold_ms back to 12 on the affected routes for the next hour while we test prefetch?
matt: No objection, doing rollout now to only routes matching /chat/assist and /chat/summarize for model redwood-7b-v2.
ops-bot: rollout controller: route-filtered kernel-change rollback attempt scheduled at 2791234620 if guard fails.
rafael: I'll start the prefetch prototype against staging and post a short status update in this thread when ready.
Anika: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in ~40m to review the dashboard trends. :thumbsup:
